title: Confirm dialog
one_line: One question, two buttons. Used by leave match, remove friend, delete account - the danger colour lives only here.

anatomy.spec: One line of body text, specific about the consequence.
Two, side by side: safe choice on the LEFT in neutral, action on the RIGHT in go (confirm) or danger (destructive only).

motion: Standard popup open/close, faster - 140 ms - since it is a quick decision.
data: Generic, reusable component - takes a title, body and two callbacks.
do_not: Do not add a close X - the neutral button is the way out (bible 5.21).
Do not use danger for anything that is not destructive.
Do not make this component screen-specific - it is shared.
acceptance: Reused by at least three call sites (leave match, remove friend, delete account) with no duplicated code.
Danger only appears for destructive actions.
steps: 2. Confirm the component is generic and reusable, not duplicated per call site.
3. Verify no close X and correct button colours per use.
4. Capture a confirm and a destructive use. Postflight.
prompt:
Polish the Ludo NX generic Confirm dialog.

Read SCREEN_PLANS/specs/SHARED_RULES.md, UI_BIBLE/LUDO_NX_UI_BIBLE.md sections 5.21 and 2.2, and this whole file. Use only values from UI_BIBLE/tokens.json.

This is the one component every destructive or consequential action shares: small NX Card, a question as the nameplate, one line of body text, and two buttons side by side - the safe choice on the left in neutral, the action on the right in go for a confirm or danger for something destructive (danger is ONLY allowed inside this dialog, nowhere else in the app). No close X - the neutral button is the way out.

Make sure it is genuinely one reusable component wired to leave-match, remove-friend and delete-account, not three separate implementations.

Follow the 'steps' array. Finish with bible section 11 and the 'acceptance' list.
